bugClass.title: Transient service failures end polling prematurely
bugClass.cause: Polling treats a failed service call caused by temporary unavailability or no response as a terminal result instead of retrying within a bounded wait. A refusal or other definitive response may still terminate polling.
bugClass.criteria: Include a site when a polling or wait loop can end, fail cleanup, skip subsequent checks, or lose a result after a transient service-call failure without bounded retry. Each mechanism qualifies independently: a call that the service never answered is treated as terminal, or a refusal is treated as retryable when it should be terminal.

candidates.evidence: Lines 139–149 poll pairing status until a 20-second deadline, but `pairing.poll(pending)` is awaited without a transient-error catch or retry path. A temporary service-call failure therefore exits the loop and skips remaining checks; cancellation is explicitly checked, and status `requested` is the only result that continues polling.

`AgentHttpAdapter.ts` lines 81–87 catches polling-call failures, emits `pollingFailure`, and deletes the active run and returns when the event is `failed`. The loop retries after 350 ms only for non-failed events; whether transient failures are classified as `failed` is not shown, so that part of the cause is unconfirmed.

Lines 54–59 reject immediately if sending fails, and otherwise settle the pending acknowledgment as failed when its timer expires. A command with no response therefore ends the wait instead of retrying; the timer bounds the wait but no retry is visible in this excerpt.

`TrackerSupervisorService.ts` lines 43–48 starts worker poll promises and cleans them up in `finally`, but the excerpt does not show how an individual polling failure is handled or whether it can end a worker after a transient service failure.

Lines 82–87 show the push loop catches `link.push()` failures, records an error, and continues while not aborted; no backoff is visible for push. The excerpt begins before the pull loop’s catch/backoff logic, so it does not establish whether a transient failure terminates polling.

Lines 97 onward show `#drainPush()` repeatedly obtains batches and awaits a network `#request`; the excerpt ends before request-failure handling or any outer retry loop, so it does not establish whether a transient failure ends polling.

The shown catch closes the callback and rethrows if opening the verification URL fails (lines 41–47); this is a handoff-launch failure, not a service-call result from a polling loop. The excerpt does not show whether polling itself retries transient errors.

`DesktopRunService.start` establishes an abort controller and enters a `try` while acquiring a repository lease and preparing a run (lines 47–60). The excerpt does not show a polling loop or how transient service-call failures affect subsequent checks.
Lines 52–65 define transient gateway and connection failure codes, but the excerpt does not show a polling or wait loop, how these errors are handled, or whether retries are bounded.

Lines 76–90 show a scheduled tick polling each due source, collecting errors, and throwing an aggregate afterward. They do not show `poll`’s service-call behavior or whether a transient failure skips bounded retries.

Lines 166–178 decide whether to record a failed run or queue a retry, but this excerpt does not show a polling/wait loop or identify whether `failure.outcome` represents a transient service-call failure.

Lines 17–20 show a timed wait whose completion unsubscribes and resolves; the visible `try` catches cleanup errors and rejects. The excerpt cuts off before the subscription/error handling, so it does not establish how a transient service-call failure affects polling.
Lines 17–19 show remote availability and project-list calls, but no wait/poll loop or failure handling is visible in the excerpt; whether a transient failure terminates polling cannot be established.
`HubHome.svelte` line 14 shows `onMount`, but the excerpt contains no polling call, failure handling, retry behavior, or relevant guard.
